title: Quotients by initial parts of a system of parameters have the expected dimension
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], meaning that $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal. Let $d\geq0$ be an integer equal to its Krull dimension $\dim A$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Suppose $a_1,\ldots,a_d\in\mathfrak m$ generate an ideal $J=(a_1,\ldots,a_d)$ with $\sqrt J=\mathfrak m$, where $\sqrt J=\{b\in A:b^N\in J\text{ for some integer }N\geq1\}$. Then for every integer $i$ with $1\leq i\leq d$ one has $\dim\bigl(A/(a_1,\ldots,a_i)\bigr)=d-i$.

from.place: Proof Step 1: dimension-normalized Verdier duality and the middle t-structure; the finite-coefficient potential-dualizing construction, via the normal-local top-residue-class input (ILO XVII Lemma 3.5.8): normality of completion and connectedness of punctured principal slices. Specific input: The prime-avoidance slicing construction in the complete-local connectedness input, retaining points in the two clopen pieces; the zero-piece case treats an empty complement. Auxiliary fact at the slicing step: choose points in the prescribed locally closed pieces which are closed in the whole punctured spectrum (Stacks 02J6(4)). Proof of the closed-point input, final contradiction: Stacks Properties 02IM(1) invokes Algebra 02IG on the quotient by the locally closed point. Proof of Stacks 02IG: after lifting parameters from R/xR, permute them and apply 02IE to the first one and first two parameters.
